Source: IATA (2024c), U.K. Department of Transport (2023) (high scenario) Among the SAF pathways, PtL SAF shows the most volatility in pricing because of escalating costs due to the uncertainty around energy pricing and availability. Shown in Table 6, near-term estimates for 2030 PtL SAF costs range widely: from as low as $8.80/gal to more than $18/gal. This high variance in production cost rises from the assumptions applied for the cost of CO and 2 electricity. Specifically, the cost to capture CO is often modeled as low as about $30/tonne for 2 high-purity sources to $800–$1,000/tonne in the case of direct air capture. A study evaluating the build- out of SAF plants necessary to meet demand determined that it would require 5,000 to 7,000 facilities with capacity of about 32 million gallons per facility, and a capital cost of $12/gal (ICF 2021). The capital investment is lower for converting petroleum refineries or renewable diesel facilities to produce SAF; various press releases and news articles point toward potential costs: • Phillips66 converted their Rodeo, California, facility to process 50,000 barrels/day of biomass into 800 million gallons per year of SAF, renewable diesel, and other products. It was projected to cost $850 million in 2022 but ultimately cost $1.25 billion (Phillips66 2022; Perkins 2024). This suggests a capital investment of $1.56/gal. • Diamond Green Diesel plant in Port Arthur, Texas, converted 50% of their renewable diesel capacity to SAF—235 million gallons per year (Valero 2024).
